content:
The image shows soybean seeds held in a hand. Key visual features:
- Seeds are the affected plant part (seed/grain)
- Most seeds are normal yellow/tan color
- Several seeds show distinctive **purple/violet discoloration** — patches ranging from small spots to large blotches covering much of the seed coat
- The purple staining is irregular in shape and distribution across different seeds
- Some seeds appear completely normal yellow, others have partial to extensive purple staining

This is a classic presentation of **Purple Seed Stain** — caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*, which produces a purple to violet discoloration on soybean seed coats. The pattern (irregular purple blotches on otherwise normal-colored seeds) is the hallmark symptom.

Note: "Cercospora" in this dataset typically refers to leaf symptoms (Cercospora leaf blight), while "Purple_Seed_Stain" is the seed-specific manifestation. The image clearly shows seed symptoms, not leaf symptoms.

Multiple seeds show varying degrees of purple staining against a yellow background, with no leaf symptoms visible."}
